data.name: Ied
data.gender_notes: Ied is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Ayd', meaning 'night'. This name is associated with the tranquility and beauty of the night sky. The name Ied carries the meaning “Night” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Ied usually hope their child will grow to embody night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey towards enlightenment and self-discovery, as well as the importance of introspection and reflection.
data.etymology: Ied belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ied total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: عيد
in_arabic.meaning: اسم من أصول عربية يعني الحج أو المولد
in_arabic.long_meaning: يعود اسم عيد إلى الكلمة العربية العيد، التي تعني الحج أو المولد. ويستخدم هذا الاسم في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحج، حيث يتحدث عن عيد النحر في سورة البقرة، ويعتبر من أشهر أسماء الله تعالى. في الإسلام، يعتبر الحج وعيد النحر من أقدس الأمور، والسماء والارض يهتفان بسم الله الأكبر في يوم عيد النحر. ويتمتع اسم عيد بالتسمية العالية في الثقافة العربية الإسلامية، ويتمتع بالكثير من الأهمية والرمزية في الحياة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: عید
in_urdu.meaning: عربی اصولو سے تعلق رکھنے والا نام ہے جو حج یا ولادت کو کہا جاتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام عید کی اصل کہانی عربی زبان کی کہانی سے ملتی ہے۔ یہ نام عید کی کہانی سے اخذ کیا گیا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے حج یا ولادت۔ آپ کی طرف سے مذکورہ نام کا استعمال قرآن میں حج کے حوالے سے کیا گیا ہے اور یہ ایک قابل ذکر نام ہے۔

in_hindi.name: ईद
in_hindi.meaning: अरबी मूल से यह नाम है जिसका अर्थ है त्योहार या पैदावार
in_hindi.long_meaning: ईद नाम का अर्थ है त्योहार या पैदावार। यह नाम अरबी भाषा से आया है। ईद नाम का उपयोग कुरान में त्योहार के संदर्भ में किया गया है।

in_pashto.name: عید
in_pashto.meaning: پښتو اصولو سې دغه نوم يې عربي پوهېدل دي چې حجه دي
in_pashto.long_meaning: نوم عيد د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی چې په معنی یې په عربي ژبه د حج پوهېدل دي. د عيد نوم په عربي کوراني متن کې د حج په اړه ويل شوی. د عيد نوم په پښتو کې په عربي ژبه د حج پوهېدل دي. د عيد نوم په پښتو کې د حج په اړه د پوهېدلو په معنی یې څرگنده ده. د عيد نوم د پښتو کوراني متن کې د حج په اړه ويل شوی.

in_english.name: Ied
in_english.meaning: Arabic origin name meaning celebration or birth
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ied originates from the Arabic root word 'aed', which means celebration or birth. In Islamic tradition, the name Ied is associated with the celebration of Hajj and Eid al-Adha. The name Ied is of great significance in Islamic culture and is often given to children born during the month of Hajj.

data.cultural_impact: Ied refers to the holiday of Eid-ul-Fitr, which marks the end of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan. This celebration is characterized by community gatherings, feasting, exchange of gifts and greetings, and dressing in new clothes.
data.spiritual_significance: Eid-ul-Fitr signifies the end of a period of self-discipline, reflection, and growth through the practice of fasting during Ramadan. This holiday offers an opportunity to express gratitude for God's guidance, strengthened faith, and renewed commitment to virtuous actions. Eid-ul-Fitr serves as a reminder to continue good deeds and to help those in need, fostering a spirit of compassion and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Ied is the Indonesian name for Eid al-Fitr, which marks the end of Ramadan, the Islamic holy month of fasting.
The term 'Ied' also refers to Eid al-Adha, another important Islamic holiday commemorating the willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son Ishmael when God asked him to do so.
historical_references.time_period: 10 days after Hajj pilgrimage in the Islamic lunar calendar

modern_usage.modern_context: Ied, also known as Eid al-Fitr, is the Islamic holiday marking the end of the holy month of Ramadan. The celebration is characterized by feasting, gift-giving, and visiting family and friends. In the modern context, social media platforms are used extensively to share updates, photos, and messages during Ied. Hashtags such as #IdulFitri, #EidMubarak, and #SweetEid are commonly used on Twitter, Instagram, and Snapchat to spread the joy of the occasion and connect with others celebrating around the world.
